title: Nifty rises 147 points despite Asian sell-off; Banks, FMCG support Sensex - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
FMCG led sectoral gains, rising 1.87%, followed by banking and financial services, while Pharma and Metal fell 1.53% and 1.50%, respectively.

Equity benchmarks closed higher on Monday despite a sharp sell-off across Asian markets, as buying in banking and FMCG stocks and sustained foreign investor inflows supported frontline indices. However, weakness in mid- and small-cap shares indicated that the recovery remained concentrated in select large-cap stocks, even as global concerns over technology valuations, inflation and interest rates persisted.

The Nifty 50 advanced 146.80 points, or 0.58 per cent, to close at 25,291.10, while the Sensex gained 512.34 points, or 0.63 per cent, to settle at 82,104.79. Bank Nifty outperformed, rising 541.80 points, or 0.89 per cent, to 61,575.90, approaching its previous record high of 61,764.

The Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100, however, declined 0.51 per cent and 1.10 per cent, respectively. FMCG led sectoral gains, rising 1.87 per cent, followed by banking and financial services, while Pharma and Metal fell 1.53 per cent and 1.50 per cent, respectively. Auto and Realty stocks also witnessed selling.

The domestic market’s resilience came against a weak Asian backdrop, with Taiwan’s Taiex falling 6 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi declining 3.6 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei losing 2.4 per cent. The sell-off was led by technology stocks amid concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence-related investments, ahead of Nvidia’s quarterly results on Tuesday. Weak Chinese industrial output and retail sales data, alongside Japan’s economic contraction in the third quarter, added to investor caution.

“The AI correction is not conclusively over,” said Hemant Sood, Founder and Managing Director, Findoc Group, adding that the technology sell-off had spread to Asia’s supply chain. He said India’s relative resilience was supported by foreign money rotating into domestic equities, but cautioned that the country’s valuation premium over other markets would need to be justified through earnings delivery. He also flagged weakness in copper prices amid concerns over Chinese demand, with the Nifty Metal index declining around 1.5 per cent.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) continued to support domestic equities, recording net purchases of approximately ₹5,737 crore on Friday, their tenth consecutive session of buying. November purchases have reached around ₹79,000 crore, according to provisional exchange data. The rupee appreciated around 0.3 per cent to close at ₹93.92 against the US dollar, while Brent crude traded around $95.40 a barrel, down 0.4 per cent. Gold remained under pressure amid a stronger dollar and elevated US Treasury yields.

Domestic inflation remained a concern, with wholesale price inflation rising to 12.29 per cent year-on-year in October from 11.39 per cent in September, largely due to higher fuel and power prices. Nevertheless, corporate earnings provided support, with Nifty 50 companies reporting 27 per cent year-on-year profit growth in the September quarter, the highest in 17 quarters, according to Motilal Oswal Financial Services.

“The next phase of market performance is likely to be increasingly driven by earnings delivery rather than valuation expansion,” said Agrim Verma, Co-founder of Divitiae Investments and smallcase Manager.

For the coming sessions, investors will track Nvidia’s results, developments from the scheduled Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, global interest-rate signals and foreign fund flows and US retail sales data alongside Federal Reserve minutes are due mid-week. Domestically, the RBI’s December 4 policy decision remains the key date, with both inflation readings now above its upper threshold.
